extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to and reviewers for Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) grant programs
extracted.subtask_short: CZI AI use in grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how applicants and reviewers may use generative AI tools in preparing and evaluating CZI grant proposals, including permitted uses, prohibitions, and responsibilities to protect confidentiality and ensure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of generative AI by applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI encourages the use of AI tools throughout the application development and preparation processes. Generative AI tools have the potential to facilitate various tasks, such as concept generation, translation, syntax review, and summarization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may use AI to assist with drafting and preparation (examples: concept generation, translation, syntax review, summarization), but should be aware of risks such as bias and hallucinations. Use must also comply with all other CZI application policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility and accountability for submitted content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who decide to use AI tools bear the sole responsibility for the content of their applications and must ensure the accuracy, coherence, and overall realistic nature of the submitted content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if AI assisted or generated parts of an application, the applicant is fully responsible for verifying and ensuring correctness and realism of content before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI use by applicants (not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI does not require applicants to disclose the use of generative AI tools in grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are informed to consider that grant applications may partly include AI-edited or generated content and to review proposals under that assumption; applicants therefore need not indicate AI involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching principles: integrity, confidentiality, privacy, and individual accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of generative AI tools should ensure the integrity and confidentiality of the grantmaking process, protect user privacy, and preserve the individual accountability and responsibility of each applicant and reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both applicants and reviewers should choose practices and tools that uphold these principles when using AI in any stage of proposal preparation or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidentiality and tool-grade requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to adhere to confidentiality terms that would apply to the use of external tools, including AI tools. Reviewers are not permitted to utilize non-enterprise-grade AI tools that do not protect applicant and data privacy or confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before participating in review, reviewers will be required to confirm their understanding and compliance with these confidentiality and tool-security requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on replacing the evaluative process with AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not permitted to utilize the tools to replace the evaluative process (i.e., generating a full automated review or scoring an application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted reviewer uses are limited to assistance such as content summarization and making feedback more readable and constructive; AI must not perform the substantive evaluation or produce final scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted reviewer tasks using AI (summarization and clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may use permitted AI tools for content summarization, such as summarizing the aims, methodologies, expected outcomes, and significance of a project, or to make their feedback to CZI more readable and constructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed uses are illustrative (summarizing aims/methods/outcomes/significance) and intended to help reviewers communicate their assessments more clearly—not to substitute for their judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibility to verify AI outputs and explain feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers that leverage AI tools must review outputs for accuracy and bear the sole responsibility and accountability for their review, and may be asked to further explain or articulate their feedback on a grant proposal in writing or verbally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using AI-generated summaries or text does not relieve reviewers of the duty to validate content; reviewers should be prepared to justify or restate their assessments without reliance on the AI artifact.

rubrics_metrics.name: No individual feedback from CZI on unfunded proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI does not provide individual feedback to applicants on decisions for unfunded proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect or rely on receiving AI-related or other detailed individualized feedback from CZI if their proposal is not funded.
